text.p: Finnish households could offer work corresponding to over 50,000 jobs, according to a study published on Monday by the economics department at the University of Turku.
In total, households capacity to employ is 108,000 people, but all of this could not be materialised without risks for the public sector, the study said.

"Employment could even be improved by an annual work input of over 50,000 people. The calculations have been made with an annual income of slightly over 100,000 markka, so this is not about low-wage work," the university said in a statement.
The study was made in cooperation with the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT).
The study said two thirds of household work now made by outsiders was in the grey economy and that the tax wedge prevents household employment.
It said the average wage offered for household work is 43 markka per hour, including social security contributions, while the average net income demand is 38 markka.
However, 43 markka per hour from the employers pocket would only amount to 26 markka in hourly net income for the employee, it said.
"This 26 markka net income per hour is less than the so called norm level, i.e. the income guaranteed in practice to everyone living in Finland," it said.
